topics.title: Data analysis foundations
topics.description: Build practical foundations through linked English resources and original practice.
topics.target_outcome: Complete and explain the listed practice tasks.

image.alt: Analytics dashboard on a laptop screen.

steps.title: Spreadsheets practice
steps.criteria: Create a five-row household budget with a SUM total. Change one expense and verify the total updates.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain how a formula differs from a typed total.

quiz_json.question: Which statement helps with this Spreadsheets practice?
options: A formula recalculates when its inputs change.
A typed total always updates itself.

quiz_json.question: How should you check your Spreadsheets result?
options: Compare the result with the stated practice criteria.
Assume it is correct without checking.

quiz_json.question: What should your Spreadsheets reflection record?
options: An example, its result and a remaining limitation.
An unsupported claim of job readiness.

steps.title: SQL practice
steps.criteria: Write SELECT, WHERE and GROUP BY queries for a small fictional sales table. Compare each result with a hand calculation.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain which rows pass your WHERE condition.

quiz_json.question: Which statement helps with this SQL practice?
options: WHERE filters rows before grouping.
WHERE invents missing records.

quiz_json.question: How should you check your SQL result?
options: Compare the result with the stated practice criteria.
Assume it is correct without checking.

quiz_json.question: What should your SQL reflection record?
options: An example, its result and a remaining limitation.
An unsupported claim of job readiness.

steps.title: Statistics practice
steps.criteria: Calculate the mean and median of five values, then add an outlier and explain how both measures change.
steps.unlocks_text: Choose a summary measure and explain its limits.

quiz_json.question: Which statement helps with this Statistics practice?
options: An outlier can change the mean more than the median.
The mean and median must always be equal.

quiz_json.question: How should you check your Statistics result?
options: Compare the result with the stated practice criteria.
Assume it is correct without checking.

quiz_json.question: What should your Statistics reflection record?
options: An example, its result and a remaining limitation.
An unsupported claim of job readiness.

topics.title: Accessible web foundations
topics.description: Build practical foundations through linked English resources and original practice.
topics.target_outcome: Complete and explain the listed practice tasks.

image.alt: Code editor and web design workspace.

steps.title: HTML practice
steps.criteria: Build a page with a heading hierarchy, a navigation link and a labelled input. Explain the purpose of each semantic element.
steps.unlocks_text: Identify the accessible name of your input.

quiz_json.question: Which statement helps with this HTML practice?
options: A label tells people what an input requests.
A placeholder replaces every label.

quiz_json.question: How should you check your HTML result?
options: Compare the result with the stated practice criteria.
Assume it is correct without checking.

quiz_json.question: What should your HTML reflection record?
options: An example, its result and a remaining limitation.
An unsupported claim of job readiness.

steps.title: CSS practice
steps.criteria: Style that page with a flexible layout. Check it at 320px and 960px and remove horizontal overflow.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain one layout change at the narrow width.

quiz_json.question: Which statement helps with this CSS practice?
options: Flexible widths help a layout fit a narrow viewport.
A fixed desktop width fits every screen.

quiz_json.question: How should you check your CSS result?
options: Compare the result with the stated practice criteria.
Assume it is correct without checking.

quiz_json.question: What should your CSS reflection record?
options: An example, its result and a remaining limitation.
An unsupported claim of job readiness.

steps.title: Accessibility practice
steps.criteria: Navigate the page using only a keyboard. Record focus order and fix one unclear label or invisible focus indicator.
steps.unlocks_text: Describe the issue and how you checked the fix.

quiz_json.question: Which statement helps with this Accessibility practice?
options: Visible focus helps keyboard users locate their position.
Keyboard users do not need a focus indicator.

quiz_json.question: How should you check your Accessibility result?
options: Compare the result with the stated practice criteria.
Assume it is correct without checking.

quiz_json.question: What should your Accessibility reflection record?
options: An example, its result and a remaining limitation.
An unsupported claim of job readiness.

topics.title: Python service foundations
topics.description: Build practical foundations through linked English resources and original practice.
topics.target_outcome: Complete and explain the listed practice tasks.

image.alt: Developer working with code on a laptop.

steps.title: Python practice
steps.criteria: Write a function that validates a list of numbers and returns their total. Show a valid input, an empty list and an invalid input.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain how your function handles invalid input.

quiz_json.question: Which statement helps with this Python practice?
options: Validate an input before calculating with it.
Assume every input is valid.

quiz_json.question: How should you check your Python result?
options: Compare the result with the stated practice criteria.
Assume it is correct without checking.

quiz_json.question: What should your Python reflection record?
options: An example, its result and a remaining limitation.
An unsupported claim of job readiness.

steps.title: API Development practice
steps.criteria: Describe GET and POST endpoints for a fictional reading list. Write example requests, responses and a validation error without using personal data.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain how the error response helps a client correct its request.

quiz_json.question: Which statement helps with this API Development practice?
options: An HTTP method communicates the request intent.
Every operation must use the same HTTP method.

quiz_json.question: How should you check your API Development result?
options: Compare the result with the stated practice criteria.
Assume it is correct without checking.

quiz_json.question: What should your API Development reflection record?
options: An example, its result and a remaining limitation.
An unsupported claim of job readiness.

steps.title: Testing practice
steps.criteria: Write tests for the number-total function covering normal, empty and invalid inputs. Introduce a deliberate bug and show which test detects it.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain what the failing test demonstrates.

quiz_json.question: Which statement helps with this Testing practice?
options: A boundary case can reveal a bug missed by a normal example.
Passing one normal example proves every input works.

quiz_json.question: How should you check your Testing result?
options: Compare the result with the stated practice criteria.
Assume it is correct without checking.

quiz_json.question: What should your Testing reflection record?
options: An example, its result and a remaining limitation.
An unsupported claim of job readiness.

topics.title: Digital foundations
topics.description: Build confident computer, internet, collaboration and online safety habits before choosing a specialist track.
topics.target_outcome: Use essential digital tools responsibly and explain your workflow.

image.alt: Learner using a laptop for online study.

steps.title: Computer Basics practice
steps.criteria: Create a folder structure for a learning project, save two files and explain how you would find them again.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain how files, folders and search support organized work.

quiz_json.question: Which action supports organized computer use?
options: Name folders clearly and save files where they belong.
Save every file with the same name.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Open the file from its folder and describe the path.
Assume the file is saved without checking.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: One example, its result and a remaining limitation.
A claim that no more practice is needed.

steps.title: Internet Research practice
steps.criteria: Compare two web pages about the same topic. Record publisher, date, purpose and one reason you trust or question each page.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain why source context matters before using information.

quiz_json.question: Which clue helps evaluate a web source?
options: Publisher, date and purpose.
Only the first search result position.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Compare evidence across more than one source.
Copy a claim without reading the page.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: A source you accepted and a source you questioned.
A list of links without notes.

steps.title: Online Safety practice
steps.criteria: Create a checklist for recognizing a suspicious message. Include sender, link destination, urgency and requested information.
steps.unlocks_text: Identify one sign of a risky message and a safer next action.

quiz_json.question: Which request deserves caution?
options: A message demanding passwords or urgent payment.
A message that asks you to verify through a known official channel.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Inspect sender and link destination before acting.
Click first and decide later.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: One risky signal and a safer response.
Private passwords or secret codes.

topics.title: Full-stack web foundations
topics.description: Connect frontend, backend, databases and deployment concepts through small practical builds.
topics.target_outcome: Build and explain a small data-backed web feature.

image.alt: Web application code on a monitor.

steps.title: Web UI practice
steps.criteria: Build a small form with labels, validation help text and a responsive layout.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain how the interface guides a user through the task.

quiz_json.question: What makes a form easier to use?
options: Clear labels and validation feedback.
Hidden inputs with no explanation.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Use the form at narrow and wide widths.
Only view it on one desktop size.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: A usability issue found and fixed.
A screenshot without explanation.

steps.title: Backend Routes practice
steps.criteria: Design GET and POST routes for the form. Include success and validation-error examples.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain how the client and server divide responsibilities.

quiz_json.question: What should a validation error do?
options: Tell the client what must be corrected.
Expose unrelated server details.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Test both valid and invalid requests.
Test only the happy path.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: One request, one response and one limitation.
A claim that every API works the same way.

steps.title: Database Records practice
steps.criteria: Sketch a table or model for the form data, including required fields and one uniqueness or validation rule.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain how stored data differs from temporary screen state.

quiz_json.question: What belongs in a database design note?
options: Fields, required rules and relationships.
Only the button color.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Try duplicate or missing data examples.
Assume every row is valid.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: A rule that protects data quality.
Private learner information.

topics.title: Cloud and DevOps foundations
topics.description: Learn deployment, environment configuration, monitoring and repeatable operations without paid infrastructure assumptions.
topics.target_outcome: Explain a small application's runtime, release and recovery path.

image.alt: Networked earth and cloud infrastructure concept.

steps.title: Environment Configuration practice
steps.criteria: List local, test and deployed settings for a small app. Mark which values are secrets and which are public.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain why configuration should not be hard-coded.

quiz_json.question: Which value should be treated as a secret?
options: A production signing key.
A public app name.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Confirm required settings fail closed when missing.
Let the app guess production defaults.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: One configuration risk and mitigation.
The secret value itself.

steps.title: Deployment Basics practice
steps.criteria: Write a release checklist covering build, migrations, health check and rollback note.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain the difference between code passing tests and a deployed service working.

quiz_json.question: What belongs in a release checklist?
options: Build, migration and health-check evidence.
Only a commit message.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Record actual command results.
Assume deployment succeeded.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: A rollback or recovery note.
A promise of guaranteed uptime.

steps.title: Monitoring Basics practice
steps.criteria: Define one health signal, one error signal and one stale-job signal for a small learning app.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain why a silent failed job needs separate evidence.

quiz_json.question: Which signal helps detect a stale schedule?
options: A recorded last-success time.
A note that the job should run.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Describe expected and failed states.
Watch only successful logs.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: One alert limit to avoid noise.
Learner secrets in logs.

topics.title: Cybersecurity foundations
topics.description: Practice defensive security basics for accounts, web requests, privacy and incident response.
topics.target_outcome: Recognize common risks and document safe handling steps.

image.alt: Security monitoring screens in a dark operations room.

steps.title: Account Security practice
steps.criteria: Compare password, session and recovery risks for a small account feature. List one safer control for each.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain why recovery flows need the same care as login.

quiz_json.question: Which control supports account security?
options: Hashing passwords and rotating sessions.
Storing passwords in readable text.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Review login, logout and recovery behavior.
Only test registration.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: A risk and a control.
A real password.

steps.title: Web Request Safety practice
steps.criteria: Map one unsafe write request and one unsafe fetch request. Explain how validation changes the risk.
steps.unlocks_text: Identify a boundary where untrusted input must be checked.

quiz_json.question: Which input should be treated as untrusted?
options: A URL supplied by a feed or user.
Only text typed into a password field.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Try allowed and rejected examples.
Accept every remote destination.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: One validation rule and why it exists.
Remote response body secrets.

steps.title: Incident Notes practice
steps.criteria: Write a short incident note with timeline, impact, fix, validation and remaining risk.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain how evidence-based notes support safer follow-up.

quiz_json.question: What belongs in an incident note?
options: Timeline, impact, fix and validation.
Blame without evidence.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Tie each claim to an observation.
Write only assumptions.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: A remaining risk or follow-up.
Unredacted secrets.

topics.title: AI and data literacy
topics.description: Learn practical AI concepts, data quality habits and responsible evaluation without paid AI dependencies.
topics.target_outcome: Evaluate AI-assisted output and explain its limits.

steps.title: Data Quality practice
steps.criteria: Inspect a tiny dataset for missing, duplicated or confusing values. Record one cleaning decision and one uncertainty.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain how data quality affects conclusions.

quiz_json.question: Which issue can affect analysis quality?
options: Missing or duplicated values.
Clear column names.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Record what changed and why.
Silently edit data.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: One uncertainty you could not resolve.
A guarantee that the dataset is perfect.

steps.title: AI Output Review practice
steps.criteria: Compare an AI-assisted answer with two trusted sources. Mark one useful part and one unsupported claim.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain why AI output needs independent verification.

quiz_json.question: What should you do with an unsupported AI claim?
options: Verify it before relying on it.
Treat it as automatically true.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Compare against trusted sources.
Ask the same tool to agree with itself.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: A useful part and an unsupported part.
Private or sensitive prompts.

steps.title: Responsible Use practice
steps.criteria: Write rules for when not to enter personal data into an AI tool and when to seek human review.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain one boundary for safe AI assistance.

quiz_json.question: Which boundary supports responsible AI use?
options: Do not enter private data into unapproved tools.
Paste every learner record for convenience.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Identify sensitive data before using a tool.
Decide after sharing it.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: A review boundary and reason.
A copied private dataset.

topics.title: Product and UX foundations
topics.description: Practice user-centered problem framing, simple flows, usability checks and product evidence.
topics.target_outcome: Design and test a small user workflow with clear evidence.

image.alt: Design notes and interface sketches on a desk.

steps.title: Problem Framing practice
steps.criteria: Write a one-person problem statement with assumptions separated from evidence.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain why assumptions need validation.

quiz_json.question: What should be separated in a product brief?
options: Assumptions and verified evidence.
Every idea and every fact mixed together.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Label which claims are assumptions.
Present assumptions as research.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: One assumption to validate.
A claim of measured impact without data.

steps.title: User Flow practice
steps.criteria: Sketch the steps a learner takes from choosing a pathway to completing one checkpoint.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain where a user might get stuck.

quiz_json.question: What does a user flow show?
options: Steps, choices and possible blockers.
Only the final screen color.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Walk through the flow with a scenario.
Skip the first and last steps.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: One place to simplify the flow.
A hidden instruction users cannot see.

steps.title: Usability Check practice
steps.criteria: Ask one person to complete a small task or rehearse it yourself with a checklist. Record one issue and one change.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain how observation changed the design.

quiz_json.question: What should a usability note include?
options: Task, observation, issue and change.
Only a personal preference.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Observe the task from start to finish.
Only ask whether the app looks nice.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: One design change tied to evidence.
A guarantee all users will succeed.

topics.title: Career readiness
topics.description: Prepare honest portfolios, applications and interview practice around demonstrated skills.
topics.target_outcome: Present one learning project and a credible next-step plan.

image.alt: People reviewing work together at a table.

steps.title: Portfolio Evidence practice
steps.criteria: Write a short project note with goal, your contribution, result, evidence and limitation.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain a project honestly without overstating readiness.

quiz_json.question: What makes portfolio evidence credible?
options: Specific work, result and limitation.
A vague claim of expertise.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Link each claim to an artifact or result.
Add claims you cannot support.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: One improvement you would make next.
A false job title.

steps.title: Application Materials practice
steps.criteria: Draft a short CV or profile summary that connects one project to one target opportunity.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain the match between a skill and an opportunity requirement.

quiz_json.question: What should an application summary connect?
options: A demonstrated skill and a target requirement.
Every unrelated interest.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Compare your summary with the opportunity wording.
Send the same text everywhere without review.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: One gap you still need to address.
A hiring guarantee.

steps.title: Interview Practice practice
steps.criteria: Answer one behavioral or project question using situation, action, result and lesson learned.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain a real example clearly and briefly.

quiz_json.question: What should a project answer include?
options: Situation, action, result and lesson.
Only tools you have heard of.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Practice aloud and time the answer.
Read silently once and stop.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: One clearer way to explain your work.
Confidential employer information.

topics.title: Entrepreneurship and freelance readiness
topics.description: Practice validating a small service idea, pricing work and communicating scope responsibly.
topics.target_outcome: Describe a small paid or volunteer service offer with clear scope and evidence.

image.alt: Small team planning business work around a laptop.

steps.title: Service Offer practice
steps.criteria: Write one narrow service offer for a real type of client, including what is included and excluded.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain why narrow scope is easier to deliver well.

quiz_json.question: What makes a service offer clearer?
options: Included and excluded work.
A promise to do everything.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Ask whether the result and boundary are clear.
Avoid defining the deliverable.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: One risk in the scope.
A guaranteed income claim.

steps.title: Pricing Basics practice
steps.criteria: Estimate time, costs and a simple price range for the service. State what would change the estimate.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain why assumptions affect price.

quiz_json.question: What should a basic estimate include?
options: Time, costs and assumptions.
Only a random final number.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: List what could change the estimate.
Hide uncertainty from the client.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: One assumption to confirm.
A promise of profit.

steps.title: Client Communication practice
steps.criteria: Draft a short message that confirms the deliverable, timeline, next step and one open question.
steps.unlocks_text: Explain how clear communication reduces rework.

quiz_json.question: What should a client confirmation include?
options: Deliverable, timeline, next step and open question.
Only a greeting.

quiz_json.question: How should you check this skill?
options: Verify the client can see what happens next.
Leave all decisions implied.

quiz_json.question: What should your reflection include?
options: One possible misunderstanding to prevent.
Private client data.
